item.title: Canada, France open consulates in Greenland in challenge to US' Arctic ambitions
item.description: Ottawa and Paris open consulates in Nuuk to support local government amid Trump's territorial claims on mineral-rich Arctic island.

item.title: Netanyahu says 'Epstein did not work for Israel', but new files citing FBI docs suggest otherwise
item.description: Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu claims ties between billionaire American pedophile and former premier Ehud Barak "doesn't suggest Epstein worked for Israel".

item.title: US and India unveil framework for interim trade deal but many details remain unclear
item.description: Full legal text of deal isn't out yet while Indian opposition Congress claims the deal is largely pro-US and harms Indian farmers and agriculture sector.

item.title: Trump says US had 'very good talks' with Iran in Oman
item.description: Trump says more talks with Tehran are due next week but warns of "consequences" without nuclear deal.

item.title: Australia warns protesters against disrupting Israeli President Herzog's Sydney visit
item.description: Herzog's Sunday visit sparks controversy, with human rights lawyers and activists calling for his arrest over Gaza genocide.

item.title: US plans Gaza peace summit to discuss reconstruction, next phase of truce — report
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has accepted the US president’s invitation for Israel to join the Board of Peace, but has not yet signed its charter.

item.title: Crypto firm accidentally sends $44 billion in bitcoins to users
item.description: Bithumb said it mistakenly distributed over $40 bn worth of bitcoin in a promotion, briefly triggering a sharp selloff.

item.title: China extends gold buying spree for 15th month in January
item.description: China extended its gold buying streak to a fifteenth month in January, increasing its holdings to 74.19 million troy ounces amid significant market price fluctuations and rising demand for safe-haven assets.

item.title: Cuba cuts workweek to four days to battle severe energy crisis amid fuel crisis
item.description: Cuba announced emergency energy-saving measures, including a four-day work week and fuel restrictions, blaming US sanctions for worsening shortages.

item.title: Pentagon cuts military education ties with Harvard over ideological dispute
item.description: The Pentagon said it will cut all academic ties with Harvard from the 2026–27 school year, citing concerns over “woke” ideology.
